text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
-- President Jacques Chirac is in Bucharest to support the entry of Romania into the European Union and NATO.
-- Technology-sharing agreed between futures and options markets Matif, CME and Nymex.
-- Compagnie Bancaire posts a 1.23 billion franc loss for 1996.

-- Korea's Daewoo Electronics Co chairman Soonhoon Bae in an interview says he does not rule out bidding for Thomson Multimedia, adds its restructuring plans are insufficient considering its competitive environment. Moreover, a planned recapitalisation would take place only after privatisation, he thinks.
-- Thomson-CSF and General Electric Co Plc widen alliance to missile guidance systems.
-- Club Mediterranee leisure group may post losses for 1996 today, analysts expected a profitable year.
-- Generale des Eaux real-estate subsidiary CGIS expected to post a 1.6 billion franc operating loss for 1996.
-- Computer services companies expected to hire some 7,000 engineers and technicians to implement software modifications for the future use of euro.

-- Turbulence ahead for Air France as staff of former Air Inter prove reluctant about the merger, which is to begin on April 1, before becoming final on September 1. Chairman Christian Blanc's goal is to have the group privatised by mid October. Former Air Inter is expected to post a loss for 1996 estimated between 800 million and 1.2 billion francs.
--True North Communications Inc and Publicis SA agree to settle all outstanding differences concerning the dissolution of a global business alliance.
